title: The wheat and the tares: who is gathered first?
opening_question: At the harvest the householder says: "Gather ye together first the tares … but gather the wheat into my barn." Who is gathered first, when, by whom, and what does Scripture say comes before that day?

steps.question: Who sowed the tares, why did the householder say not to gather them up yet, and what is gathered first at the harvest?

facts.text: "Tares" is the Greek zizanion, "darnel or false grain". The Ethiopian Canon reads "darnel weeds" and the BSB "weeds".
The householder: "Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them." Then: "Let both grow together until the harvest".
"First" in "Gather ye together first the tares" is the Greek proton, "firstly (in time, place, order, or importance)".

steps.question: In Jesus' own explanation, who is the sower, what is the field, who are the reapers, and when is the harvest?

facts.text: "The harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels". "End" is the Greek sunteleia, "entire completion", and "world" is aion, "properly, an age". The Ethiopian Canon and the BSB read "the end of the age".
"The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity", and cast them "into a furnace of fire".
After the tares are gathered: "Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father".

steps.question: In the parable of the net and in John the Baptist's words, who is separated from whom, and where does each go?

facts.text: "So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just".
John the Baptist: he will "gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire".

steps.question: In the days of Noah, whom did the flood take away? Then who "shall be taken" and who "left", and where else is the same Greek word for "taken" used?

facts.text: Matthew 24:39: "the flood came, and took them all away". "Took" there is the Greek airo, "to take up or away". The BSB reads "swept them all away"; Luke 17:27 says the flood "destroyed them all".
"Taken" in "the one shall be taken, and the other left" is a different word, paralambano, "to receive near". Jesus uses it in John 14:3: "I will come again, and receive you unto myself".
"Left" is the Greek aphiemi; the KJV also translates it "forsake", "leave" and "forgive".

steps.question: Lot's wife, one taken and one left: when the disciples asked "Where, Lord?", what did Jesus answer? Whom do the angels gather in Matthew 24:31?

facts.text: Jesus answered: "Wheresoever the body is, thither will the eagles be gathered together". The Ethiopian Canon reads "vultures", and the BSB "Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather".
Luke 17:36 ("Two men shall be in the field") is in the KJV; the Ethiopian Canon and the BSB have no verse 36 there.
Matthew 24:31: "they shall gather together his elect from the four winds".

steps.question: Who rises first, who is caught up, and to meet whom? What did Paul tell the Thessalonians not to be shaken by?

facts.text: "The dead in Christ shall rise first", then "we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them". "First" is again proton; "caught up" is harpazo, "to seize".
Paul writes "by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him", that they "be not soon shaken in mind".

steps.question: What must come first before that day, how does the man of sin come, and why do they who perish believe a lie?

facts.text: "For that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first". "Falling away" is the Greek apostasia, "defection from truth"; the Ethiopian Canon and the BSB read "the rebellion".
"Let no man deceive you" in 2 Thessalonians 2:3 is the Greek exapatao, the word Paul uses in 2 Corinthians 11:3: "as the serpent beguiled Eve".
His coming is "after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders"; "strong delusion" is the Greek plane, "delusion, error".
Jesus: "many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many", "the love of many shall wax cold". Paul: "some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits".

steps.question: What did Jesus say to do if anyone says Christ is in the desert or in the secret chambers? How will his coming be seen, and who reaps the harvest of the earth?

facts.text: "There shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect".
"Behold, he is in the secret chambers; believe it not." Then: "as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be".
Revelation 14: one "like unto the Son of man" with "a sharp sickle", "for the harvest of the earth is ripe".
The path The rapture: what does the Bible say? reads many of the same verses from the other side. Read the two as a pair.

steps.question: The other separation parable: whom does the King set on His right hand and on His left, and what did each one do?

facts.text: "he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats".

steps.question: Living it out: the servants were told "Let both grow together until the harvest". What do these verses ask of us toward judging others, and toward our own readiness?

facts.text: "Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me"; "Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith".

remember.text: "Let both grow together until the harvest" ... "Gather ye together first the tares"
"the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels"
In Noah's days the flood "took them all away".
"that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first"
If they say He is in the desert or the secret chambers: "believe it not".
